concerns.text: T011 says 'the script raises the exception so the execution stage can off-load to a real GPU (device="cuda")'. FR-009 mandates 'any attempt to fall back to GPU must be aborted and flagged as a failure.' The task authorizes a GPU fallback path the spec explicitly forbids; remove the off-load clause and abort/flag instead.

Spec requires 20 independent runs per variant (40 total); plan commits to 20 per variant per environment (120 total, seeds 42-61). T014 executes only 5 seeds (30 runs) and T015 is written for an 'N = 5 bounded data regime'. This silently relaxes the sample size underpinning SC-003's power claim with no documented spec amendment.

concerns.text: T012 introduces a teacher fallback chain (Qwen2.5-7B 8-bit, falling back to 3B) that appears in neither spec nor plan (plan names only Qwen2.5-0.5B and a <7 GB RAM constraint). A 7B 8-bit teacher plus student and retriever will exceed the plan's own memory budget; the substitution is authorized only by the task itself.

T007 requires the schema to include per-step 'peak_memory_mb', but the read-only contract names the per-step field 'step_peak_memory_mb' (reserving 'peak_memory_mb' for the run summary). Implementing T007 as written produces a schema that conflicts with the contract-mandated field naming.

FR-002 mandates a fixed 10,000 training steps and SC-002 defines the cost comparison over a 'fixed 10,000-step horizon'. T003 uses a 'reduced step cap, e.g. 200 steps' and T014 uses early stopping with a 6-hour-budget cap; the cost-only sub-phase in T014 carries no step count. No artifact preserves the 10,000-step figure the spec requires.

The FR-to-task coverage map omits FR-008 (recording Success_Baseline per environment for SC-001) entirely, even though the plan maps it to Phase 3. No task explicitly guarantees the baseline success metric is recorded for the SC-001 comparison.
The plan's Phase 0b pilot correlation gate (2k-step baseline runs, Pearson r >= 0.4 go/no-go before the main study) has no corresponding task, so a committed plan constraint is silently dropped.

Plan and tasks add Bonferroni correction, making the effective alpha stricter than the spec's plain p < 0.05; this tightening is undocumented in the spec. Either document it in the spec or drop it from the tasks.

The plan's runner-pinning measures (recording lscpu / psutil.cpu_freq per job, verifying <5% hardware variance as a covariate for SC-002) have no implementing task, so the CPU-time measurements SC-002 depends on lack the controls the plan promises.
